$comment: Tile headlines and ledes for the Atlas cards (owner points 1, 15, 16, 18 Oct 2026). Each line restates only what its cited rows say: a place title comes from its own sheet's 'why' row, a region or Spain line from the places listed in 'from'. Draft until the owner OKs it.

spain.lede: From Atlantic rain in the green north to volcanic ash in the Canaries, Spain grows its wine on slate terraces, chalk plains and the albariza of Jerez. Pick a region and fly in.

green-spain.title: Atlantic rain, slate terraces and Albariño
green-spain.lede: Spain's wet Atlantic edge. Getaria gets about 1,600 mm of rain, vines climb slate and granite terraces above the Miño and Sil, and the whites come out bright and high in acid, from Albariño to txakoli.

castilla-y-leon.title: A high plateau, hard winters, Tempranillo built to age
castilla-y-leon.lede: High, hard continental country. Rueda sits at 700 to 870 metres, Toro's old bush vines ride out harsh winters, and Ribera del Duero's Tempranillo gains the balance and sweet tannin to age.

rioja.title: Where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean
rioja.lede: Atlantic and Mediterranean climates meet here, with about 400 mm of rain. Rioja Alta leans Atlantic, Rioja Oriental runs drier and warmer, and the reds are made for ageing.

ebro.title: The dry cierzo wind and slow-ripened reds
ebro.lede: The dry cierzo wind shapes this region. In Campo de Borja it keeps the vines short of water, so they ripen slowly into deep-coloured, aromatic wines; Navarra adds limestone and freshness.

cataluna.title: Slate slopes, sea influence and old Garnacha
cataluna.lede: From the sea to the mountains. Priorat's steep slate gives deep-coloured reds high in extract, Montsant's old Garnacha and Cariñena grow sheltered from the sea, and wild herbs give Pla de Bages aromas of rosemary and thyme.

mediterranean.title: Monastrell and Bobal on dry, chalky plateaus
mediterranean.lede: Hot, dry and chalky. Monastrell makes broad, fleshy reds in Jumilla and Yecla, Bobal gives deep red, high-acid wine in Utiel-Requena, and the sea air keeps Alicante fresher than its inland neighbours.

meseta.title: Sun-struck plains: 3,000 hours of sun on chalk
meseta.lede: Spain's great central plateau. La Mancha gets 3,000 hours of sun and only 300 to 350 mm of rain, Almansa sits high on limestone, and Campo de Calatrava grows on dark volcanic soil.

andalucia.title: Albariza, flor and the solera
andalucia.lede: The south of flor and solera. Jerez plants on albariza that holds moisture, sea air feeds the flor in Manzanilla, and Málaga dries grapes in the sun for sweet wines.

baleares.title: Island vines cooled by the salty Embat
baleares.lede: Two island DOs. In Pla i Llevant the salty Embat wind cools vines at sea level under strong sun; in Binissalem local grapes ripen in full.

canarias.title: Native grapes on volcanic ash, behind stone walls
canarias.lede: Wine on volcanic islands. Lanzarote grows native grapes in volcanic ash on 150 mm of rain, Tenerife's slopes fall from Teide to the coast, and El Hierro's terraces run from 50 to 1,000 metres.
